facts.raw_span: A 32-year-old primigravida at 36 weeks 3 days of gestation presented with acute left lower abdominal pain and vomiting
She denied vaginal bleeding, urinary symptoms, constipation, or changes in bowel habits
On examination, there was slight tenderness in the left abdomen without guarding; the uterus was soft and relaxed
Foetal movements and monitoring were normal
a 70 × 60 × 60 mm left ovarian cyst first noted at 5 weeks and thought to be endometriotic
Follow-up scans at 32 weeks showed the cyst measured 63 × 33 × 69 mm with internal echoes and an avascular solid component
Tumour markers (CEA, CA-19-9, CA-125) were within normal limits
Hb was 121 g/L, WCC 10.0 × 10^9/L, neutrophils 9.1 × 10^9/L, platelets 270 × 10^9/L, and CRP 30 mg/L
CRP rose to 209 mg/L while WCC remained stable
Repeated transabdominal and transvaginal ultrasounds by an experienced sonographer showed the left adnexal cyst unchanged in size and appearance
At 37 weeks 1 day, her pain worsened with vomiting, and abdominal exam revealed generalized tenderness with guarding in the left iliac fossa
Given the acute abdomen, rising inflammatory markers, and concern for ovarian torsion, the decision was made to proceed with a caesarean section followed by surgical management of the adnexa
